items.headline: Tech is priced for shrinking earnings while Q3 profits grew 53%
items.summary: After last week’s AI-infrastructure flush, @ParadisLabs argued investors are now positioned as if tech companies were reporting negative earnings growth, against actual Q3 tech earnings growth of 53% in aggregate and 35% for the median company, and called it a reasonable spot to start rebuilding longer-term positions. @oguzerkan noted the tech sector’s P/E is the lowest since the 2020 Covid crash, blaming fears that the capex-driven boom is cyclical. @aleabitoreddit pushed back on the “AI bubble” label altogether, pointing to memory makers at 1–3x forward earnings and optical names like $POET trading below net cash.
items.short: Positioning implies negative tech earnings; Q3 grew 53%. Tech P/E lowest since 2020.

items.headline: Sacks: permitted data centers get built in 2027; he’s “really worried about 2028”
items.summary: On the All-In fallout from Tuesday’s midterms, David Sacks said fully permitted projects should still be finished in 2027, but he expects few major new ones after that because no one has a political incentive to grant new permits. Chamath argued a slowdown would make the hyperscalers kingmakers, squeezing neoclouds and model labs that rent capacity. Not everyone agrees: Rosenblatt called the result a “relative non-event” for Nebius, whose big planned US sites are in Missouri, Pennsylvania and South Carolina, not the states that flipped.
items.short: Sacks: 2027 builds safe, 2028 at risk; Chamath: hyperscalers become kingmakers.

items.headline: Apple’s own Xcode plugin lands in Claude Code
items.summary: A plugin authored by Apple now sits in Anthropic’s official Claude Code marketplace, letting the agent build, run and test iOS apps, render SwiftUI previews and drive simulators from the terminal. @gregisenberg turned it into a playbook: find high-revenue utility apps rated under 3.5 that haven’t shipped an update in six months, then build a better one with agents.
items.short: Apple-authored Xcode plugin ships in Claude Code’s marketplace.

items.author: GREG ISENBERG
items.text:
I think the coolest part of having kids is reliving your own childhood in a different way.  

You remember what it felt like to be scared of the dark, to wait all year for a birthday or to think a cardboard box was the best toy in the world. 

The difference is that now you're on the other side of it. And you get to be the person who makes those moments feel safe and magical.

You see the world through someone who's seeing it for the first time, and it makes you curious again. 

I didn't expect parenting to make me feel younger on one hand, and older on the other but some days it does.

Highly recommend :)

quoted.author: bayes
quoted.text:
We need to stop using generic terminology. AI is not a monolith. There are critical things we need to do with AI for economic prosperity, there are things we may have to do for reasons of national competition, there are things we will at some point need to do carefully for the sake of charting and taming the computational universe, and there are things we should totally avoid doing at this stage of history, and maybe ever, if at all possible. 

If we can’t be precise about these issues because we’re saying vague things like “using coding agents to make AI progress should be illegal”, then we risk failing altogether. Each of the goals above depends on achieving the others. 

If we can’t prosper we can’t lead the world into the future. Everyone needs to internalize this. Democrats cannot subjugate themselves to antigrowth. Republicans cannot subjugate themselves to technocapital. Both roads lead to despair.

items.author: Serenity
items.text:
I'm going to give a contrarian take on Neoclouds like $NBIS and say the theme looks compelling after the valuation crash. 

Since there's a reason why Elon's $SPCX is heavily focused on this market full of "guppies" that would die: 

He sees how attractive the economics are after selling compute to $GOOGL and Anthropic. 

And this is reflected by his actions not words, from SpaceX's recent $40B financing for GPUs procurement. 
$AMZN, $MSFT, and even $META also see how profitable the economics are and are accelerating their AI DC buildouts. 

I'd argue if a Neocloud has: 

- Close relationships with $NVDA + others for allocations
- Existing contracted capacity + permitting
- Well funded counterparties, such as Hyperscalers. 
- Attractive economics, such as financing their procurement correctly (not the way $CRWV has with high debt interest unless they refinance). 

Then I think they'll do just fine... 

However, the bigger worry is more toward newer players starting financing or the permitting process, since barrier to entry has now become extremely high. 

For financing, read through on $IREN earnings has shown public Neoclouds can adapt extremely well to tight markets:

As seen with their 90% prepayments for GPU capex on a 5Y deal. 

Their older H100 GPUs recontracted at double their previous pricing and 12% higher contracted pricing also point against depreciation fears. 

And in the case DC buildouts slow from permitting delays... it heavily favors some over others. 

Rosenblatt's recent note for example stated they see little risk with $NBIS primary buildout that was in Missouri, Pennsylvania, and South Carolina. 

And there's probably less risk with developers in places like Australia. 

Markets have also show this infinite compute arbitrage can't go on forever, hence the reluctance to further finance capex, via things like ATMs. 

But ironically, tighter financing and hypothetical restrictive permitting would increase the competitive advantage of established neoclouds. 

And create a larger moat against newer DC developers.

items.author: Jim Liu
items.text:
$IREN's Advantage in the Neocloud Race

There's more to IREN popped 20% on Friday than the  228m revenue and announced 22m/MW long term deals and 40m/MW short term deals. If you study the after hour price action, you'd see IREN stock lost considerable gains on the announcement of H2 delays even though it was MSFT's change request but regained the loss on the announcement of their FY 2027 funding strategy.

Datacenter Backed Financing

$IREN currently has 9B in "cash, undrawn GPU financing facilities, and contracted customer prepayments" (1). $IREN needs $15B capex for FY 2027 so astute investors might be questioning where they will get the remaining 6B. 

On the earnings call IREN has stated they have 6B of unencumbered billing datacenters and will have 10B once H2-4 and rest of Mackenzie and B300s in Childress (2 - picture 1). Of their 15B of GPUs, 6B are unencumbered as GPUs bought with previous convertibles and ATMs.

Datacenter Assets > GPU Assets in Stability

The Datacenter assets are stronger for financing than the GPUs. To show the appetite for DC assets, on Nov 3, DCRU sold 3 North American Datacenters to DLR at 5.2-6.6% cap rates or 21m-26m/MW (3). DLR is essentially a datacenter REIT and they are buying datacenters that were built pre-2000. 5.2-6.6 cap rates are incredible for pre-2000 DCs and clearly shows for safe assets like DCs! 

In historical of overcapacity in silicon chips, silicon chips without datacenters are massive negative cashflows, even at negative profit, all extra silicon needs datacenters to make the negative profit manageable. So all this Elon scare of financing drying up for GPUs backed financing, does not hold for DCs backed financing.

Own the Assets = Flexibility to Adapt

IREN has also stated that they are only using ATM opportunistically and that they have also slowed down their Capex spend on developing the further out sites in their pipeline and have the flexibility to stop their ATM (1).

Asset Heavy is Not So Expensive

Once you understand that capex used for the initial generation of DCs once billing can be used to financing future DC buildouts, you understand the flywheel. Then IREN basically gets save on both colocation and potential BE fuel cell costs in their final margins!

$CRWV does not have DC assets and $NBIS only has Finland which is small relative to their market cap. $IREN will have 10B of DCs relative to their 10B market cap! At 50%-70% LTC, this means IREN can access half their funds equal to more than half market cap without diluting! In times like this, wall street absolutely loves that and it's a big part of $IREN's 20% move on Friday.

Once shorts realize they cannot rely on ATM shares to cover their short positions, IREN will an ignited recovery. 

Everything Is Relative

At less than 1/3 the market cap, $IREN has much less growth expectations than $CRWV, $NBIS which also means it needs to expand less which means it needs less Capex and $IREN is in the unique position that it's DC asset base is equal to it's market cap and if you count it's 6B of unencumbered DCs, $IREN has access to 12-15B of financing. 

*Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 Refers to July 2026-June 2027.

items.headline: A six-to-twelve-month drug course may cure a common cause of high blood pressure
items.summary: In a small NEJM study led by Queen Mary University of London, 14 people with primary aldosteronism took aldosterone synthase inhibitors for 6–12 months. Up to two years after stopping, the hormone marker stayed 99% below baseline and blood pressure averaged 25 points lower; a larger trial, ELIXIR, is under way.
items.short: NEJM: temporary aldosterone-synthase inhibition gave lasting BP drops in 14 patients.

items.headline: Lp(a)-lowering drug fails its big heart-outcomes trial
items.summary: Novartis’s pelacarsen cut lipoprotein(a) by about 78% in 8,350 people with heart disease but did not reduce heart attacks or strokes over five years, researchers reported at the American Heart Association meeting. One possibility now on the table: high Lp(a) may be a marker of risk rather than a cause.
items.short: Pelacarsen cut Lp(a) 78% but didn’t prevent cardiac events.

items.headline: High-dose flu shot linked to 55% lower Alzheimer’s risk
items.summary: UTHealth Houston researchers analyzing nearly 200,000 adults 65 and older found high-dose flu vaccination associated with a nearly 55% lower Alzheimer’s risk, versus about 40% for the standard dose. It is an association, not proof of cause.
items.short: High-dose flu vaccine tied to ~55% lower Alzheimer’s risk (observational).

items.author: sridhar

His conclusion: watch paid GPU use, price per unit and firm obligations, because a capacity bust is more likely than a bank run.

items.rule: If a parcel is marked Express, it has a red sticker.
items.explanation: Express could hide something that breaks the rule; No sticker breaks it if the other side turns out to be Express. Most people pick the card that matches the rule's second half instead of the one that could falsify it.
